title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 1st District
area: Northeast Tennessee, including Kingsport, Bristol, and Johnson City

context.text: Incumbent Diana Harshbarger (R) advanced unopposed from the August 6, 2026 Republican primary. Kristi Burke won the Democratic primary. The district's 2026 Cook Partisan Voter Index is R+29, and forecasters rate the general election Safe/Solid Republican.

candidates.name: Diana Harshbarger
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the August 6, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Diana Harshbarger is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 1st District, a licensed pharmacist and former pharmacy business owner from Kingsport.

background.text: Born in Bloomingdale, Tennessee; earned an undergraduate degree from East Tennessee State University and a doctorate in pharmacy from Mercer University College of Pharmacy.
Worked as a licensed pharmacist and business owner, and served as a board member of the International Academy of Compounding Pharmacists.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (2025-2026), including its Subcommittees on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Health; and Energy.

summary.text: Kristi Burke is the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 1st District, running on a platform centered on healthcare access and economic fairness for East Tennessee.

background.text: Says she was raised with a religious upbringing that taught her to 'care for the vulnerable,' and describes herself as living without health insurance under what she calls a 'pay or pray' system.

priorities.text: Says essential needs like healthcare, housing, and a clean environment should not be gatekept by wealth, and frames her campaign as a challenge to policies that prioritize corporate interests over working residents.

positions.summary: Campaign message emphasizes that healthcare should not depend on wealth and says no one in the district should be 'one medical emergency away from ruin.'
positions.quote: I believe that essential needs like healthcare, housing, and a clean environment, should never be gatekept by wealth.

summary.text: Joshua Ray Ashburn is an independent candidate who says he supports term limits, stronger border security, and reduced U.S. involvement in foreign conflicts.

priorities.text: Says he strongly supports term limits and putting 'the people first instead of politics.'

positions.summary: Says maintaining secure borders is essential and that border security should remain a top priority to reduce drug trafficking.
positions.quote: I strongly believe that maintaining secure borders is essential to the safety, stability, and well-being of our country.

summary.text: Chris Campbell is an independent candidate from East Tennessee running on a platform of manufacturing jobs, patient-directed healthcare, and opposition to tariffs.

background.text: Says he has spent his professional career supporting manufacturers and grew up watching factory closures affect his family in Appalachia.

priorities.text: Wants to restore domestic manufacturing and 'reshoring' of industries, and supports patients' rights to pursue treatments their providers recommend without insurer denial.

positions.summary: Says tariffs have made housing, energy, groceries, and transportation more expensive and supports abolishing them.
positions.quote: These are fueled by tariffs (taxes) that were unconstitutionally imposed on Americans and a war that we should have never taken part.

summary.text: Richard Baker is a perennial independent candidate who has run for this seat in multiple previous elections (2020, 2022, and 2024). No campaign platform statements were found for the 2026 race.
Billy Cody is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for Tennessee's 1st District. No campaign website or public policy statements were found.
Tyler McClain is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for Tennessee's 1st District. No campaign website or public policy statements were found.
